display_name: Sher Shah Suri & Rao Maldev Rathore
one_line: Afghan emperor Sher Shah Suri and Rajput ruler Rao Maldev Rathore facing off in the harsh plains near Giri-Sumel, 1544 CE.

appearance.age_look: Sher Shah appears in his early 50s, sturdy and broad-shouldered; Rao Maldev appears in his late 30s to early 40s, tall and athletic.
appearance.face: Sher Shah has a square, weathered face, wheat-brown complexion, strong nose, neatly trimmed dark-grey beard and moustache, with sharp, assessing eyes and a calm, firm default expression; Maldev has an oval face, sun-browned Rajput complexion, straight nose, neatly groomed black moustache with light stubble on the jaw, large expressive eyes and a focused, proud default expression.
appearance.hair: Sher Shah’s hair is kept short and mostly hidden under a plain conical Afghan turban-helmet: a quilted dark-green fabric cap wrapped with a cream cloth band and a small mail aventail peeking at the edges; Maldev’s hair is black, tied back in a small knot at the nape under a saffron-orange Rajput pagri with a slight forward tilt and a narrow red band, the turban fabric draping slightly at one side.
appearance.costume: Sher Shah wears a quilted, knee-length dark-green cotton qaba (long coat) with vertical stitching, fitted at the waist with a plain brown leather belt, over a light-cream long-sleeved tunic and loose, narrow-at-ankle brown churidar trousers, plus a sleeveless steel breastplate with simple rivets over the chest; his forearms have plain brown leather bracers, and he wears dark-brown leather boots reaching mid-calf; a simple dark-cream wool shawl is wrapped around his shoulders when at rest, and he has a small string of wooden prayer beads wrapped around his left wrist. Rao Maldev wears a long-sleeved, knee-length angarkha in deep indigo blue with wrap-over front tied at the side, subtle block-printed floral motifs in a slightly lighter blue, and a narrow red piping at the edges; beneath is an off-white cotton tunic and tightly wrapped off-white churidar; over the angarkha he wears a polished steel breastplate shaped to the torso, with minimal engraved lines, and a matching simple steel vambrace on his left forearm; he has a dark-maroon cloth kamarband (waist sash) with a visible knot at his right hip and a small dagger’s hilt peeking from it, and he wears brown leather jutti-style shoes with upturned toes.
appearance.signature: Sher Shah carries a slightly curved Indo-Afghan talwar with a plain steel blade, dark-brown leather-wrapped hilt and simple disc pommel, sheathed in a dark-brown scabbard hanging from his belt on his left; Rao Maldev carries a distinctive Rajput talwar with a slightly broader, gently curved steel blade, a brass hilt with a knuckle-guard and disc pommel, and a deep-red leather scabbard slung from his right hip over the maroon sash.

ref_desc: Sher Shah Suri is a sturdy, wheat-brown, square-faced man with a neat dark-grey beard, short hair under a dark-green Afghan turban-helmet, wearing a quilted dark-green qaba, cream tunic, brown churidar and steel breastplate with brown boots and plain talwar, while Rao Maldev Rathore is a tall, sun-browned Rajput with an oval face, black hair in a knot under a saffron-orange pagri, indigo blue angarkha with subtle patterns, off-white churidar, maroon waist sash, simple steel breastplate, brown jutti shoes and a brass-hilted Rajput talwar in a red scabbard.
sheet_prompt: Draw two full-body anime-style model sheets side by side showing Sher Shah Suri and Rao Maldev Rathore in 1544 CE on the plains of Rajasthan, with clear front and three-quarter views. Sher Shah Suri is a sturdy, wheat-brown, square-faced man with a neat dark-grey beard and moustache, sharp eyes and a calm, firm expression; his short hair is mostly hidden under a quilted dark-green conical Afghan turban-helmet wrapped with cream cloth and a hint of mail at the edges. He wears a knee-length, quilted dark-green cotton qaba with vertical stitching over a light-cream long-sleeved tunic and brown churidar trousers, a sleeveless steel breastplate with simple rivets, plain brown leather bracers on his forearms, and dark-brown mid-calf leather boots; a simple dark-cream wool shawl can be shown draped loosely around his shoulders in one view, and a small loop of wooden prayer beads is wrapped around his left wrist. His signature weapon is a slightly curved Indo-Afghan talwar with a plain steel blade and dark-brown leather-wrapped hilt, in a dark-brown scabbard hanging from his belt on his left. Rao Maldev Rathore stands tall and athletic with an oval face, sun-browned complexion, large expressive eyes and a proud, focused expression; his black hair is tied in a small knot at the nape under a saffron-orange Rajput pagri with a narrow red band and a slight drape on one side. He wears a deep indigo blue knee-length angarkha with a wrap-over front tied at the side, subtle lighter-blue block-printed floral motifs and thin red piping at the edges, over an off-white tunic and tightly wrapped off-white churidar. Over this is a polished steel breastplate with minimal engraved lines and a simple steel vambrace on his left arm; at his waist is a dark-maroon cloth kamarband with a visible knot and a small dagger hilt, and on his feet are brown leather jutti shoes with upturned toes. His signature weapon is a Rajput talwar with a slightly broader, gently curved steel blade, brass hilt with knuckle-guard and disc pommel, in a deep-red leather scabbard slung from his right hip. Emphasise historically grounded fabrics and armour, clear, saturated colours of dark green, cream, indigo blue, saffron orange and maroon, and maintain consistent anime-style proportions and details so the two rulers can be redrawn identically in many panels.
